correctness.rationale: The labeled icosahedral graph and its 264 open-neighborhood simplices are unambiguous. Exact full-boundary eliminations over F2 and F3 give ranks 11,49,48,12 and Betti numbers (1,0,23,0,0) mod 2. Connectivity, universal coefficients and Euler characteristic 24 determine rational H0=Q, H2=Q^23, all other rational H vanish. Exhaustive graph-automorphism backtracking enumerates 120 permutations and a normal 60-element rotational subgroup generated by all order-five elements; the canonical antipode is central and splits the group. Signed simplicial Lefschetz traces for all 120 automorphisms determine the full rational H2 character; projection by (1±iota)/2 and exact A5 character inner products yield W6+V5 in the even part and 2*trivial+2*V5 in the odd part. The packaged exact standalone verifier has been replayed successfully. No inference from a partial finite sample to an infinite claim and no inference from mod-two Betti numbers to an integral representation is made.

originality.rationale: The closest published same-object homotopy calculation establishes only a nonequivariant wedge of 23 two-spheres; this is explicitly credited and not the new theorem. That information does not determine the full A5×C2 rational homology action, especially the antipodal parity and absence of full-group invariant classes. Matsushita supplies an equivariant graph-topology formalism but not the specialized icosahedral character; Shukla covers other degree restrictions and nonequivariant homotopy. Searches under alternative box/Hom terminology found no statement implying the decomposition. Residual risk of obscure prior equivariant calculations is retained.

value.rationale: The regular icosahedron is a canonical symmetric graph and the full order-120 automorphism action is a natural, functorially induced invariant of its Lovasz neighborhood complex. Determining the complete rational 23-dimensional A5×C2 representation goes beyond the known nonequivariant homotopy type: it separates 11 even and 12 odd homology classes, locates exactly two rotation invariants and proves no full symmetry invariants survive. This precise symmetry question is motivated by equivariant box and Hom graph topology, not by an arbitrary parameter choice; integral equivariant refinements remain future mathematical questions.
